question.text: Mr. Aditya Rao (Manager, Yarlung AIF) is told by an LP DDQ that his PPM shows a 'super-carry' of 25% above a 3x MOIC, versus industry 20% above 2x. The LP's DD team wants the structure justified. The COMPLETE Manager defence, per Ch 12's framing, is:

answer.text: Cite our premium pedigree — no quantitative justification needed.

Justify via (a) track-record outperformance and reputation supporting a premium fee/carry structure, (b) acknowledge that super-carry is acceptable where it is negotiated IN LIEU OF a higher management fee (per footnote 126), (c) be open to a management-fee concession to balance the overall economics.
Argue that super-carry always reduces the LP's net-of-fee IRR compared with standard carry.
Claim that super-carry is required under SEBI (AIF) Regulation 15A.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 12, higher fee structures should be justified by past performance and reputation. A lower management fee combined with a higher incentive (super-carry) may be preferred by some institutional investors, and footnote 126 expressly supports super-carry in lieu of a higher management fee. The Trap: Option A offers no justification. Option C overstates the impact of super-carry on net IRR in absolute terms. Option D fabricates a regulation. Note: The trade-off framing — track record plus management-fee versus carry mix — is the workbook's source-backed defence of premium economics.
